recommendations.rationale: Advisory only, and adoption alone executes nothing. The consumed check shows the recorded input at the update-32 saved state ended 0.01 s at a materially higher projected tip speed than the available braking-box input, so the plan objective not penalizing residual tip speed (recorded holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0) is a candidate to revisit. No value is derived from the single 10 ms probe and no closed-loop or multi-step evidence establishes that changing it would fix settling.

Defer any dominant-cause or causal claim: one 0.01 s projected-model comparison at a single saved state cannot rank objective weighting, solver early-stop plan quality, or projected-versus-backend mismatch, and no closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal attribution capability exists in this inventory.

Defer further local separation of the weighting and early-stop mechanisms until the non-retained historical full warm plans / optimizer iteration traces (control_snapshots.json) are available; the authorized check budget (max_checks 1) is spent and no further check is authorized in this workflow.

attribution.reason: At this one saved projected state the recorded applied input ended 0.01 s at a materially higher projected tip speed (1.4501 m/s near-endpoint) than the braking-box arm (0.6433 m/s), so the recorded command did not use all locally available braking authority over this step. This is a local, projected-model, single-state, 10 ms observation; it does not establish a closed-loop settling cause or dominance.

This form of H2 predicted that bounded local braking authority would make the braking box's endpoint speed close to the recorded input's. The observed endpoints differ materially (0.6433 vs 1.4501 m/s), so that specific prediction is not observed. The separate observation that the box saturates two channels at the 8 N limit shows the authority is finite, which is a different statement from authority being unavailable.

Even the maximal braking-box arm remained at 0.6433 m/s, far above the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit, at the end of one 10 ms step, so no input within this box settles the projected tip in a single step. This bounds one step only; it makes no claim about a multi-step or held-input braking policy, and the result's own interpretation warns that instantaneous deceleration need not persist.

Recorded holding_tip_speed_weight is 0.0 with small velocity terms, consistent with a plan objective dominated by position tracking that reaches position while residual speed persists. The probe cannot separate this weighting mechanism from solver early-stop plan quality because both predict the same local endpoint.

Nearly all sampled updates ended by policy stop rather than Solve_Succeeded, mean update wall time is 17.075238 s, and sampled late effective horizons collapse to 3 and 1 control intervals, which is plausible under-damped short-lookahead behavior. The check result leaves this hypothesis locally indistinguishable from the weighting hypothesis, and no retained warm plans or iteration traces separate them.

The maximal braking request saturated two channels at the 8 N per-tendon inventory limit, so braking authority at this state is finite and can bind. Proximity to the limit under a synthetic maximal-braking request is not the same as the recorded plan being limit-limited, and the probe cannot rank this against the other mechanisms.

The long mean update wall time and deadline misses are compute overruns of synchronous controller calls relative to the 0.01 s control period, not an injected physical feedback delay in simulated time; they remain relevant only as a symptom of solver load. No retained or checked evidence supports a physical-delay mechanism.

Both probe arms use the projected GVS model, so the check cannot test projected-versus-backend mismatch; retained matched-interval evidence is described as recorded projected states, not full backend-state error, and no retained evidence ranks this mechanism against the command-objective and solver-quality mechanisms.

The consumed check result explicitly lists this pair as unresolved when both predict the same local endpoint, and the non-retained historical warm plans / optimizer iteration traces that could separate them are absent from the inventory.

facts.statement: Run summary: reach_passed is true with terminal tip error 0.007642609 m inside the 0.01 m reach tolerance, but sampled settling did not pass; late_max_speed_m_s 1.581015274 and late_max_error_m 0.058138104 both exceed the settling criteria (position 0.01 m, speed 0.02 m/s, window 0.05 s), and terminal tip speed 0.635172609 m/s stays above the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit. Reach success and settling failure therefore coexist in this run's summary.

Sampled solver/policy and horizon evidence: the summary stopping counts report Solve_Succeeded = 1; sampled late updates 32 and 33 both ended with optimization_raw_status 'User_Requested_Stop' (policy_stop_reason 'budget_best_feasible'), while sampled update 34 ended 'Solve_Succeeded'. Mean update wall time is 17.075238 s against a 0.01 s control period, and sampled effective horizons shrink to 3 control intervals at update 32 and 1 at update 34.

Recorded controller recipe terms: holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0, tip_speed_scale_m_s 0.02, velocity_weight 0.0001, terminal_velocity_weight 0.0001, tension_weight 0.0001, variation_weight 0.001. Raw weight magnitudes alone do not establish cost-term importance without actual term contributions.

Consumed check result at the saved projected state for update 32 (model.gvs@1.0.0, horizon 0.01 s, implicit-Euler step 0.002 s, label rows[1] 'instantaneous_braking_box_solution'): the instantaneous braking-box arm ended at projected tip speed 0.643277005 m/s at t=0.01 s, while the recorded-applied-input arm's projected tip speed was 1.450055969 m/s at t=0.008 s and 1.417890206 m/s at t=0.006 s. The braking box therefore yields a materially lower projected endpoint tip speed than the recorded input at this one saved state.

The braking-box arm applied per-tendon tension [0.0, 0.0, 8.0, 8.0, 0.0, 0.0] N, i.e. it saturated the inventory 8 N per-tendon limit on two channels, yet its endpoint tip speed 0.643277005 m/s remained far above the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit and its endpoint tip error 0.028486500 m was only slightly below its own error at t=0.004 s (0.028574185 m). A single maximal 0.01 s braking step does not bring this projected tip to settling speed.

The check result is flagged advisory_only true and ranking_changed false and reports complete_cost_s 8.567265; both arms were evaluated under model.gvs@1.0.0 at the single saved projected state for update 32 over a 0.01 s horizon. Its own unresolved list states it cannot separate the recorded 0.0 terminal/holding tip-speed weighting from solver early-stop plan quality, cannot test projected-GVS versus backend-model mismatch, and that one 0.01 s comparison cannot explain, rank, or attribute the whole closed-loop settling failure.

limitations: Model limit: all numerical comparison is under model.gvs@1.0.0 (projected GVS), not a full serial-backend replay; backend re-execution was out of scope (backend_solves 0).
Projected-state limit: the probe used a single saved projected state bound to update 32 (recorded projected state, not full backend state); the summary reports full_snapshots_available false.

Input limit: the braking arm is an analytic bounded linear objective on a unilateral tension box, not an iterative input optimizer; no closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal attribution capability exists in this inventory.
Integration limit: implicit Euler in mass/force form with a 0.002 s step; endpoint positions/velocities are integrator outputs, not measurements.

Horizon limit: a single 0.01 s horizon; the result is advisory_only and states instantaneous deceleration need not persist during a held-input rollout, so it cannot explain the whole-run settling failure.
Interpretation limit: local plan/endpoint differences at one state do not certify causality, dominance, or closed-loop settling, and raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance.

Coverage limit: the middle of the run was not displayed (backend motion 0.01-0.29 s; one-step predictions, applied tensions and projected states for the unsampled updates), and the historical full warm plans / optimizer iteration traces are not retained.
